summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and morbid obesity was admitted for acute abdominal pain and diagnosed with an incarcerated ventral hernia causing bowel obstruction. She underwent urgent surgical repair with mesh placement and adhesiolysis, then remained intubated in the ICU due to respiratory failure from underlying lung disease and pulmonary edema. She developed ventilator-associated pneumonia, treated successfully with a 10-day course of meropenem. She was extubated on postoperative day 8, advanced to a regular diet, and mobilized with physical therapy. Her heart failure was managed with diuresis, and her anticoagulation was resumed. She was discharged to rehab with a JP drain that was later removed, stable vital signs, and improved respiratory and surgical status.
